class: persistent data written outside the mounted volume
what_happened: After chromadb moved to 1.x it persisted at /data while compose still mounted the 0.x path, so the RAG store was wiped on every container recreate; a doc-watcher re-ingest masked the loss.
root_cause: The volume mount was not updated when the image's data directory changed between major versions.
lesson: The node must verify after every image upgrade or recreate that each service's persistent data path is the mounted volume and that the data survived (expected database/collection still present), and must not let an automatic re-ingest hide data loss.
tripwire: Post-upgrade check that the bitcoin_node_knowledge collection is present, plus a tar backup of the store before the live run. Should exist: a test that each service's data dir for the pinned image version matches its volume mount.
applies_to_new_node: yes — indexers, explorers and vector stores on either node can move their data dir across major versions.

class: version identity taken from an untrustworthy self-report
what_happened: Compose pins used library short names and mempool/frontend was never repinned (live v3.2.1/v3.3.1 drift); chroma's API reported version '1.0.0' forever regardless of the running image.
root_cause: Version was read from the service's own API and pin edits did not cover every image a service uses.
lesson: The node must take a service's version identity from the image reference it pinned and deployed, not from the service's self-reported version, and pin edits must be anchored to image: lines so a short name cannot match arbitrary text.
tripwire: upgradeStaleRepo tests (12) and a sanity pre-flight that rejects nonexistent tags (checkDockerHubTag both-prefix logic). The general sibling-image registry gate came later (2026-08-22-mempool-page-stale-explorer-and-zero-fees.md).
applies_to_new_node: yes — both nodes will pin container images and need one source of version truth.

class: recovery path trusted without a live drill
what_happened: One-click upgrades (verify, sanity, snapshot, repin, recreate, health, rollback) were extended to tor/redis/chromadb/mariadb behind an action-time step-up password and a zod service enum; rollback for the four new services was only code-reviewed, not live-fired.
root_cause: Rollback was assumed to work because it shared a pattern with the proven bitcoin upgrade path.
lesson: Every upgrade the node offers must run the full pipeline (verify, sanity pre-flight, snapshot, repin, recreate, health wait, automatic rollback) behind an action-time owner credential and a closed allowlist of services and version charset, and its rollback must be proven by a deliberate failed-upgrade drill before it is trusted.
tripwire: Planned monthly failed-upgrade drill (a tag that passes pre-flight but fails, or killing the container mid-health-wait). The 2026-08-22 rollback-consolidation record later found a second rollback path that had never worked.
applies_to_new_node: yes — container upgrades still need their own rollback on top of the OS image rollback.

class: privilege grants written in a dialect only one implementation parses
what_happened: Sudoers grants used argument globs (mount /dev/* /media/*, chmod [0-7][0-7][0-7][0-7] /data/*) that sudo-rs, Ubuntu 26.04's default sudo, cannot parse, which would have silently stranded every drive, backup and candidate operation after the OS upgrade.
root_cause: Privilege policy was expressed in sudoers wildcard syntax that only classic sudo accepts.
lesson: The node must grant privilege only as exact-path rules on small root-owned wrapper scripts that re-validate their arguments themselves (realpath resolution, refusal to touch the system disk, LVM-aware disk detection via lsblk -s rather than PKNAME), never as argument globs.
tripwire: bash -n on both wrappers, visudo -c on the templates, privilegedApply.test.ts for the caller switch. Per-wrapper live-fire was still open when the record landed. Should exist: a test that exercises each wrapper subcommand on a scratch device and a check that every sudoers line is an exact path.
applies_to_new_node: yes — Fedora IoT's sudo/polkit differ from Ubuntu's; exact-path wrappers (or dedicated systemd units) behave the same under any implementation.

class: hardcoded distro identity
what_happened: tailscaleService hardcoded 'stable/ubuntu/' and relied on lsb_release, which is absent on Debian minimal; the installer also lacked libnss-mdns and ufw for the USB-install target.
root_cause: Code assumed one distribution instead of reading the OS identity.
lesson: The node must derive distro and release from /etc/os-release, never from lsb_release or hardcoded names, and must declare every OS package it relies on in the image/installer.
tripwire: Code change only. Should exist: a test running distro detection against os-release fixtures for every supported OS.
applies_to_new_node: yes — moving to Fedora IoT turns every Ubuntu/apt assumption into a defect.

class: engineering evidence held only in ephemeral session memory
what_happened: The sudo-rs build session left its facts in session memory and no build record; the record and commit were written 25 days later by a different session, with per-wrapper live verification still open.
root_cause: The record was not begun at planning time and committed with the change.
lesson: Every change must carry its build record and evidence in the repository at commit time; agent session memory is not a durable record.
tripwire: Procedure rule (record committed with the change). Should exist: a pre-commit/CI check that a change to protected paths references a build record.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the new node is built with AI sessions that have the same memory failure mode.

class: consensus verdict leaks across engines through shared state
what_happened: After switching from Knots (BIP-110 enforcing) to Core, Core inherited Knots's invalid mark on majority block ...ff24ba from the shared block index, refused the majority chain and crawled the 1-2%-hashrate signaling chain (9 blocks in 10 h); its only two outbound peers were frozen Knots enforcers.
root_cause: Both engines shared one blocks/index directory, so a policy-driven invalid verdict persisted across the engine switch.
lesson: If the node supports switching consensus engines, it must detect inherited invalid-block verdicts after a switch (chaintips plus log detection), clear them only with owner authority, eject and ban peers of the divergent faction, seed fresh peers, keep maintenance mode until the new engine is at tip (with a hard cap) and report convergence; consensus actions such as reconsiderblock are never automated without the owner.
tripwire: engineSwitchPostflight.ts convergence supervisor built during the incident; not yet exercised by a real switch at record time (engine-switch drill required).
owner_decision: Owner spec for the class fix: "eject wrong-faction peers, locate the right headers, self-heal stands down during the switch, rotate peers cleanly". reconsiderblock was blocked from automation and run by the owner by hand.
applies_to_new_node: maybe — only if the new node offers Core/Knots switching or shares a datadir between engines; separate datadirs avoid the class.

class: monitor that has never succeeded, logged as noise
what_happened: The IBD monitor's bitcoin-cli call had no -datadir, so it failed with 'Could not locate RPC credentials' every 60 seconds from the day it shipped; the error had been read as background RPC noise.
root_cause: The probe built its own CLI invocation instead of using the engine- and network-aware helper, and nothing tracked that it had never produced a value.
lesson: Every monitor must record last success and must alert when it has never succeeded or stopped succeeding; repeated identical probe errors are a failed monitor, not noise. All bitcoind RPC callers must use one engine- and network-aware client.
tripwire: Fix routed through getBitcoinCliPrefix(); sibling sweep for bare bitcoin-cli docker execs (hardwareDetector the only offender). Should exist: a last-success age check on every probe.
applies_to_new_node: yes — both nodes run bitcoind monitors; the Pi's pruned node and the x86 full node need network-aware RPC config.

class: progress misread as a stall
what_happened: As part of the durable fix, the BITCOIN_SYNC_STUCK issue was changed to stand down while block height advances (catch-up is not a stall), while a failed progress probe still produces the alert so a dead bitcoind pages.
root_cause: A stall detector that does not look at progress cannot tell a long catch-up from a stall.
lesson: A sync-stuck alert must be driven by absence of height progress, not by distance from tip, and a failed progress probe must fail toward alerting.
tripwire: issueSynthesizer progress guard + syncStuckStandDown.test.ts (3 cases).
applies_to_new_node: yes — the Pi 5 pruned node will spend long periods catching up.

class: runtime default heap too small for startup reindex
what_happened: The reorg plus a 270-block catch-up gave mempool-api a startup reindex that outgrew Node's container-aware default heap (~860 MB inside a 2 GB container): fatal heap OOM, 305 restarts over ~9 hours, zero notifications.
root_cause: The runtime's default heap ceiling was below what a reindex needs, and nothing watched restart counts.
lesson: The node must size runtime memory explicitly for worst-case startup work (reindex after reorg or catch-up) within the container limit, and a crash-looping service must page the owner.
tripwire: NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1536 in compose; restart-loop detection built the same day (2026-08-10-crashloop-detection.md).
applies_to_new_node: maybe — applies where the explorer stack runs (x86 full node); the Pi 5's memory tier makes it worse.

class: recovery-by-restart looks like health
what_happened: mempool-api restarted 305 times over ~9 hours with no notification; a CONTAINER_RESTART_LOOP issue type already existed but no probe ever produced it.
root_cause: The restart policy masked the failure and no probe counted restarts.
lesson: The node must detect any service restarted more than N times in M minutes (classifying OOM/heap signatures) and notify the owner, deduplicated per service; the remediation for a looping service is diagnosis, never another restart.
tripwire: utils/restartLoopDetector.ts (pure, injected clock) + restartLoopDetector.test.ts (8 cases); dedup 1/hour/container. Proven on 2026-08-16 when it notified the owner of a recurrence within ~2 h.
owner_decision: "nothing should fail silently or be in a crash loop"
applies_to_new_node: yes — systemd units and containers on both nodes; systemd's NRestarts gives the same signal.

class: dangling reference to a remediation that does not exist
what_happened: An audit of issue metadata found five referenced runbook ids (e.g. RB-CONTAINER-DIAGNOSE-01, RB-MEMORY-INCREASE-01, RB-NGINX-RELOAD-01) that existed nowhere.
root_cause: Issue types and their suggested runbooks were authored with no check that the target exists or that any probe produces the issue.
lesson: Every alert type must have a real producer and every remediation reference must resolve to an existing runbook; detect-and-notify-only issues must say so explicitly instead of pointing at a phantom.
tripwire: Manual sweep here; automated later by runbookCommandAudit.test.ts (no hypothesis points at a missing runbook id) and drbSchemaGate.test.ts (all remediation ids resolve).
applies_to_new_node: yes — any alert/runbook catalog on the new node.

class: concurrent mutators on a shared namespace without a mutex
what_happened: After a reboot-requiring OS upgrade, four systemd units started in the same second and raced 'docker compose up' on one project ('container name /tor is already in use'); the upgrade was reported failed although apt had succeeded. A journal scan found 28 such conflicts on five days since 2026-07-01, including ordinary non-upgrade reboots.
root_cause: Every stack script shared one compose project name, compose up is not concurrency-safe, and no caller took a lock.
lesson: Stack bring-up at boot and during upgrades must go through one serialized entry point (an advisory lock released on process death), ordered with After= rather than Requires=/BindsTo= so a deliberately disabled unit cannot block the rest, and every mutator of the shared namespace (including self-heal paths) must take the same lock.
tripwire: scripts/compose-lock.sh + upgradeRebootBringup.test.ts (19 tests; 17 failed on the pre-fix tree); isolated 12-container lab: 7 conflicts without the lock, 0 with it. Live reboot verification still open at record time.
applies_to_new_node: yes — whatever orchestrates containers on Fedora IoT (podman/quadlet or compose), parallel bring-ups at boot must be impossible.

class: state that must outlive a reboot held only in memory
what_happened: Maintenance-mode alert suppression was an in-memory field reset at start, and isUpgradeInFlight() read a written result as 'finished' although the runner must write it before rebooting; the post-reboot bring-up fired CRITICAL 'Bitcoin Core is down' and 'LND is down' alerts.
root_cause: Suppression state lived in process memory and the finished signal was written before the reboot it had to span.
lesson: Upgrade/maintenance state that spans a reboot must be persisted with a bounded grace window; the window must expire and must never silence alerts on a timestamp that cannot be bounded (absent, unparseable, future).
tripwire: Pure evaluateUpgradeState(state, now) with eight grace-window cases in upgradeRebootBringup.test.ts.
applies_to_new_node: yes — rpm-ostree/greenboot reboots on both nodes need the same persisted maintenance window.

class: validator drops items with a warning nobody reads
what_happened: loadCards() silently dropped 2 of 50 concept cards (including the BIP-110 frozen-height explanation) because they lacked owner/last_reviewed; it only logged a warn.
root_cause: Invalid knowledge items were skipped with a log line instead of failing a check.
lesson: Every knowledge item shipped to the assistant must load; a dropped item must fail CI rather than log a warning.
tripwire: None added in this record; the class recurred and was gated in 2026-09-02-os-update-banner-staleness.md (conceptCardsIntegrity.test.ts).
applies_to_new_node: yes — the sandboxed assistant's knowledge store.

class: checking a condition before the state transition it is meant to observe
what_happened: A smoke run came back RED because the session's readiness loop accepted health==200 from the still-old process before systemd had begun the restart, so smoke ran mid-restart.
root_cause: Readiness was judged by an HTTP 200 that the pre-restart process could also give.
lesson: After a restart, readiness must require evidence of the new process (ActiveState=active after the restart began, a new PID or start time) as well as health.
tripwire: Gate corrected to require ActiveState=active AND health 200.
applies_to_new_node: yes — every restart-and-verify step on both nodes.

class: vacuous tests counted as regression guards
what_happened: The regression suite was re-run on the restored pre-fix tree: 17 of 19 failed; the 2 that passed were invariant assertions, vacuously true before the change, and were not counted as guards.
root_cause: A test that passes before and after a fix cannot detect the defect.
lesson: Every regression guard must be proven red against the pre-fix code (or by mutation) before it is counted; tests that pass both ways are labelled characterization.
tripwire: Pre-fix tree restore / mutation runs recorded in the evidence log (pattern repeated in later records).
applies_to_new_node: yes — the new repo's fix-lock procedure already requires a failing test first.

class: memory ceiling raised instead of bounding growth
what_happened: mempool-api crash-looped again (103 restarts), dying at ~1506 MB, exactly the 1536 MB ceiling set on 08-10, while 'Restoring rbf data from disk cache' with a 26,275-tx mempool; this time the restart-loop detector notified the owner.
root_cause: Startup memory scales with live mempool size and accumulated container-internal cache, so any fixed ceiling is eventually outgrown.
lesson: The node must bound memory growth of indexers/explorers (cache limits, periodic cache reset, or not running the full explorer on an undersized memory tier) instead of repeatedly raising ceilings, and keep the sizing history next to the setting.
tripwire: Restart-loop detector worked (owner notified within ~2 h). Fix: container 2G to 3G, heap 1536 to 2304, cache cleared by recreate; sizing history and third-strike rule documented inline in compose.
owner_decision: Standing decision recorded in the record (not quoted as the owner's words): "if this OOMs again, we STOP raising ceilings and bound the growth instead".
applies_to_new_node: maybe — the explorer on the x86 node; on the Pi 5 the record's own question (does the full explorer fit this memory tier) applies.

class: in-progress state misread as finished
what_happened: The 'Update Linux' button reported '17/17 packages still pending' while apt was in fact succeeding; the outcome verification raced the live apt run.
root_cause: systemd oneshot units report 'activating' (non-zero is-active exit) while running, and the old check treated anything but 'active' (with a swallowed throw) as not running; earlier tests used completed runs only.
lesson: The node must treat activating/deactivating/reloading as running, must never issue a verdict while the package manager lock is held or the runner is in progress, and must test outcome verification against in-progress states, not only completed runs.
tripwire: isRunningUnitState() pure helper + runnerActiveState.test.ts (3 cases; activating=running is the bug); getRunnerState reports running while the apt/dpkg lock is held.
owner_decision: Owner spec (paraphrased in the record): a live progress view until a VERIFIED end state.
applies_to_new_node: yes — rpm-ostree updates also run as units with transitional states.

class: process liveness reported as data liveness
what_happened: mempool-api's update loop silently stopped after block 963534 while the container stayed 'Up (healthy)' and served a frozen snapshot; the explorer was 120 blocks / 20.6 h behind bitcoind with no error, exception or restart.
root_cause: The container healthcheck only required a 200 from an endpoint a frozen backend answers from cache; the wedge itself was never root-caused.
lesson: Every indexer/explorer health check must compare the service's own chain tip with bitcoind's, not just HTTP liveness, and a stale-but-alive service must be a distinct alert from a dead one.
tripwire: evaluateMempoolSync() (>=3 blocks lag for 3 ticks) + MEMPOOL_SYNC_STALLED outranking MEMPOOL_API_DOWN; mempoolStalenessAndFees.test.ts (10 tests: 120-block lag fires, at-tip and 1-block race do not, unreachable explorer does not double-fire).
applies_to_new_node: yes — electrs/explorer on the x86 node and LND's chain sync against bitcoind on both nodes.

class: precision loss plus falsy zero treated as missing
what_happened: Real sub-1 sat/vB estimates (0.443/0.443/0.316) were rounded to whole sats, giving 0, and the frontend's '|| null' turned 0 into 'no estimate', so the Low/Economy/Minimum cards and the fee calculator showed '—'.
root_cause: Math.round on the sat/vB value and a truthiness test for presence.
lesson: Fee rates must keep sub-sat/vB precision end to end, absence must be an explicit null tested with ?? or !== null (never truthiness), and a missing estimate must never be invented.
tripwire: mempoolStalenessAndFees.test.ts gates the exact live numbers (0.443/0.443/0.316 must not come back as 0 or null).
applies_to_new_node: yes — low-fee regimes drive LN fee, sweep and channel-open decisions on both nodes.

class: multi-artifact service tracked by one artifact only
what_happened: mempool-web was pinned at v3.2.1 while mempool-api ran v3.3.1 for about three and a half months, so the explorer UI floored sub-1 sat/vB fees to whole numbers; the version checker knew only the backend image, so the drift was invisible.
root_cause: The checker registered one image per service and the sibling repin was a hardcoded, forward-only special case.
lesson: The node must keep one registry of every image (primary and lockstep siblings) per service, detect pin drift from what is actually on disk, and fail the build if any deployed image is unregistered; repinning is an owner decision, not a self-heal.
tripwire: SIBLING_IMAGES + getSiblingPinDrift() + hourly evaluateImagePinDrift() (IMAGE_PIN_DRIFT, no auto-runbook) + a CI test that every image: pin is registered, with a negative control.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any service shipped as more than one image.

class: targeted change executed as whole-project reconcile
what_happened: Bumping only the mempool-web tag via 'docker compose up' recreated bitcoin, electrs, mempool, redis, tor and lnd; lnd came back attached to no network (NetworkMode set, Networks {}), used the host's 127.0.0.53 resolver, could not resolve 'tor' and restart-looped until reconnected by hand.
root_cause: compose up reconciles every service in the project, and a recreated container can start without its network attachment.
lesson: Upgrading one service must recreate only that service; after any recreate the node must verify network attachment and DNS of each container, and LND must never be restarted as a side effect of an unrelated change.
tripwire: Existing restart-loop detector covers the symptom. Should exist: a post-recreate check that every container has a non-empty network set and the runtime's embedded resolver.
applies_to_new_node: yes — podman/compose on Fedora IoT; LND restarts carry channel risk once channels exist.

class: diagnostic action destroys the evidence
what_happened: Sending SIGUSR1 to the wedged mempool-api to open the V8 inspector restarted the backend (its own handler treats it as fatal), destroying the wedged state before a stack could be captured; the wedge's cause is still unknown.
root_cause: The signal's meaning in that process differed from Node's default.
lesson: Before touching a wedged process, capture its state non-destructively; services that may wedge should start with diagnostics enabled (e.g. --inspect) so evidence can be taken without a restart.
tripwire: Rule in the record: if MEMPOOL_SYNC_STALLED fires repeatedly, run mempool-api under --inspect and capture the stack instead of restarting.
applies_to_new_node: maybe — applies to whichever explorer/indexer the new node runs.

class: recovery path that only runs after a failure rots unseen
what_happened: A second upgrade-with-rollback path had never once succeeded; in production (2026-07-11) its auto-revert for DRB-ELECTRS-DOWN-01 logged 'Rollback failed:' with no reason. It called the uninstalled docker-compose v1, used a rotted image map (dead repos, literal 'undefined'), container names that never matched, and no --profile or lock.
root_cause: Two implementations of 'upgrade a container' existed and the rollback one only ever ran after something else had already broken.
lesson: The node must have exactly one apply path for upgrades and rollbacks and one module that drives the container runtime (correct binary, files, profiles, lock), and rollback must be exercised by tests and drills, not only by real failures.
tripwire: utils/composeControl.ts as the single driver + rollbackConsolidation.test.ts (16 tests: no legacy overlays, right profile per service, flock + v2 plugin, deleted methods stay deleted, failure reason interpolated).
owner_decision: Owner chose: consolidate, not repair-in-place.
applies_to_new_node: yes — container rollback still matters alongside OS image rollback.

class: layered configuration override silently downgrades a service
what_happened: Legacy overlay files pinning lightninglabs/lnd:v0.18.0-beta and mempool v3.0.0 were layered after the main compose file by the rollback path, a hand-run startup script, a guardian service and the AI command knowledge base; since later -f files win, a 'rollback' or start of LND would have downgraded it three majors regardless of the snapshot.
root_cause: Pre-profiles relic files stayed in the repo and in several command paths after the stack moved to one unified file.
lesson: The node must have one source of truth for which image each service runs; no overlay or legacy config may override a pin, and a downgrade of LND or bitcoind must never happen unless explicitly requested.
tripwire: rollbackConsolidation.test.ts asserts both overlay files do not exist; runbookCommandAudit.test.ts rejects deleted overlays in runbook commands.
applies_to_new_node: yes — a silent LND/bitcoind downgrade is a funds-adjacent risk on both nodes.

class: no-op command reports success
what_happened: Without --profile, 'compose up' on a profile-gated service (lnd, mempool-*, chromadb) matches nothing and still exits 0.
root_cause: The runtime treats an empty selection as success.
lesson: Every lifecycle command must verify its effect (the named container exists and runs the expected image) rather than trust the exit code.
tripwire: composeControl emits the profile each service needs (asserted in rollbackConsolidation.test.ts). Should exist: a post-action state assertion.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any container runtime with selective profiles/units.

class: error reason lost by logging API misuse
what_happened: logger.error('[Rollback] Rollback failed:', error.message) logged a bare prefix because the logger ignores a second argument, so the failed safety net could not say why.
root_cause: The logger's call signature did not format extra arguments.
lesson: Failure logs must interpolate the reason into the message (or use a structured field proven to be emitted), and a test must assert the reason appears.
tripwire: rollbackConsolidation.test.ts asserts the failure reason is interpolated.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the rebuilt backend's logging.

class: dead code still reachable from an installer
what_happened: scripts/install-services.sh would have run 'lsof -ti:5000 | xargs kill -9' against the live dashboard port and installed, enabled and started units for a nonexistent user that carried the LND-downgrade command.
root_cause: Legacy installer scripts and units stayed in the repo after the real installer moved elsewhere.
lesson: The node must have one installer/image definition; legacy installers and units must be deleted once proven dead (real installer, users, paths, running processes checked), not left as runnable hazards.
tripwire: Six files (1,182 lines) deleted after proof; typecheck and suite green. Should exist: a check that every unit file in the repo is installed by the one installer.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the clean rebuild should start with one image definition.

class: probe matches its own command line
what_happened: Two pgrep checks reported scripts as running because the shell command matched its own command line; the next day's runbook audit hit the same pgrep false positive plus a systemd regex that truncated unit names (17 false hits).
root_cause: Pattern-based process and unit matching did not exclude the probe itself or anchor names.
lesson: Liveness and 'is it dead' checks must use exact identities (unit state, PID, exact process name) that exclude the probe itself, and any deletion decision must be confirmed against the live system.
tripwire: Re-checked with ps -eo pid,cmd | grep -v 'zsh -c'; recorded as a method note. Should exist: shared tested probe helpers.
applies_to_new_node: yes — agents and scripts probing both nodes.

class: assistant knowledge describes nonexistent or dangerous commands
what_happened: The assistant's command knowledge base (data/commands.json) had twelve entries citing the downgrading overlays, including 'make start-lightning', and 42 of 77 entries were make targets although no Makefile exists; the assistant could have handed the owner the downgrading command.
root_cause: A generated knowledge artifact was never validated against the real tooling.
lesson: Every command the assistant can suggest must come from one validated catalog that CI checks against real scripts, units, endpoints and pins; stale or generated command stores must be deleted.
tripwire: Overlay entries removed here; the whole commands.json chain was deleted in 2026-08-23-runbook-command-audit.md, and the live catalog (command-database.json) is covered by a CI test.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the sandboxed assistant must not be able to suggest unvalidated commands.

class: auth gate and router disagree on path normalization
what_happened: GET /api/Lightning-Mobile/zeus-connection returned 200 with the admin LND macaroon (and /api/WALLET/derived-addresses and /api/Ssh/keys returned 200) without credentials while the lowercase paths returned 401; also reachable through the aggregate frontend port, including over Tailscale.
root_cause: Express routes case-insensitively by default while the auth gate compared paths case-sensitively, so a re-cased path matched no tier and fell to the loginless viewer branch.
lesson: The auth gate must classify exactly the path the router will dispatch (same normalization for case, trailing slash, encoding, dot segments), or routing must be strict; every credential route must be tested with re-cased and otherwise-normalized variants.
tripwire: apiAccessPolicy.test.ts 're-casing a URL cannot step around a tier' (5 failed on the old code); live probe table of case, percent-encoding, dot segments, double and trailing slashes.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the rebuilt backend gates macaroons, onions and wallet routes.

class: untestable inline security policy drifts from intent
what_happened: The surviving AI command executor (POST /api/ai/execute), Lightning fund routes (/lightning/pay, /lightning/channels/open, /lightning/wallet/sendcoins), AI spend limits, provider credentials and fleet-wide execution matched no tier, so in login mode a plain session JWT sufficed; /ai/execute was the same class as the /terminal and /commands RCE routes deleted earlier.
root_cause: The tier lists were inline constants inside buildApp(), so no test could import or assert them.
lesson: Security policy must live in a pure, importable, default-closed classifier tested route by route: execution, fund movement, AI spend authority, credentials and the local/cloud privacy boundary each asserted to need action-time owner auth in every auth mode, with the reads beside them asserted unaffected.
tripwire: classifyApiRequest in security/apiAccessPolicy.ts + the 'request tier classification' block in apiAccessPolicy.test.ts (65 tests at the time).
applies_to_new_node: yes — fund and execution routes on both nodes.

class: test asserts an internal label instead of the user-visible outcome
what_happened: The first version's comment said halting the AI must stay easy, but /ai/emergency-stop was on no benign list, so default-closed still demanded a password; the test asserted only the tier ('not step-up') and passed anyway.
root_cause: The assertion checked a classification label, not whether the user would actually be asked for a password.
lesson: Security tests must assert the effective behaviour the user experiences (e.g. 'this request requires step-up'), not an intermediate label.
tripwire: Re-asserted on requiresLoginlessStepUp.
applies_to_new_node: yes — policy tests in the rebuilt backend.

class: state-changing endpoint probed as a read on a live system
what_happened: Verification POSTed /api/ai/emergency-stop on the running node, which halted the AI for about four minutes and left an unmatched critical EMERGENCY_STOP_ACTIVATED audit entry because the flag was cleared by deleting the file.
root_cause: A route designed not to fail closed was probed as though it were a read.
lesson: State-changing routes must be verified through classification/unit tests; only routes already proven to fail closed (401 before the handler) may be probed on a live node.
tripwire: Rule recorded in the record; the audit trail was made self-reconciling in 2026-08-24-ai-emergency-stop-actually-stops.md.
applies_to_new_node: yes — agents verifying the new nodes must not exercise live state-changing endpoints.

class: safety brake gated behind the credential it may be needed without
what_happened: Design: /ai/emergency-stop was admitted to the benign (no-password) set while /ai/emergency-resume requires the owner's step-up.
root_cause: A brake the owner cannot reach without first finding their password is not a brake (the record's rationale).
lesson: The AI emergency stop must be reachable without a password; resuming must require the owner's action-time credential.
tripwire: apiAccessPolicy.test.ts asserts the stop/resume asymmetry on effective behaviour.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the sandboxed assistant needs a frictionless stop.

class: inter-node messages trusted on the transport gate alone
what_happened: /consensus/receive accepted peer node data with no signature check in the handler, relying entirely on the transport gate (which in loginless mode would demand an owner password, so inter-node consensus was likely non-functional); left for a design decision.
root_cause: Peer authentication was delegated to the HTTP auth gate instead of the message itself.
lesson: Messages between the owner's nodes must be authenticated by signature in the handler, independent of the HTTP auth mode.
tripwire: None — needs a design decision. Should exist: a handler-level signature test with forged and replayed messages.
applies_to_new_node: maybe — only if the x86 and Pi nodes exchange coordination messages.

class: default-closed rule not reconciled with real callers
what_happened: After every non-public mutation was made step-up gated, a theme change raised the 'this action can move funds' password modal and AI chat demanded a password per message; the public allowlist named /theme, /language and /preferences (zero callers) while the endpoint the UI actually used, /node-prefs, was absent.
root_cause: The allowlist described an app that no longer existed and was never checked against what both frontends call.
lesson: Hardening must be verified in both directions: allowlist entries are exact METHOD /path, reconciled against real callers (source and shipped bundles), with a negative table asserting dangerous siblings (execute, credentials, drive format, payments, alert-silencing toggles) stay gated; breaking a legitimate path is a defect.
tripwire: apiAccessPolicy.test.ts benign and negative tables (45 tests at the time), plus path-traversal and extra-segment refusal on the one parameterized entry.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the rebuilt UI and API.

class: chat endpoint as a mutation path in disguise
what_happened: Before letting /ai/chat run without a password, the session checked that chat auto-execution requires autoApprove && risk 'low' and that all 20 eligible commands were read-only diagnostics; free-form execution stayed at /ai/execute behind step-up.
root_cause: Chat can auto-run commands, so its authority equals the most dangerous command it can auto-run.
lesson: The assistant's no-credential surface may only auto-run commands from a fixed, reviewed list of read-only diagnostics; any free-form or mutating execution must require the owner's action-time credential.
tripwire: The 20 eligible entries in data/command-database.json were listed and reviewed. Should exist: a test that every autoApprove entry is read-only.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the sandboxed assistant's command surface.

class: UI promises a security property the code cancels
what_happened: The Terminal page rendered a password + 2FA lock that auto-unlocked whenever the nodeDashboard bypass was on (it was), while its backend executor had already been deleted; the owner reported "the authentication requirement for Terminal has not worked".
root_cause: The lock existed only in the UI and client-side logic cancelled it.
lesson: The node must never render a security gate the server does not enforce; every lock or 'authentication required' UI must correspond to a server-side tier, and a removed feature must take its routes, nav entries, locale keys and assistant knowledge with it.
tripwire: Build with the file deleted (2508 to 2506 modules) and bundle grep for unlockTerminal / System Diagnostics returning 0. Should exist: a test mapping each UI gate to a server tier.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the rebuilt UI.

class: overstated risk warning
what_happened: The Access Control warning claimed 'anyone on your network will have full access', which had been untrue since fund, execution, credential and host actions each require the owner password.
root_cause: Warning text was not updated when action-time gating was added.
lesson: Security warnings must state the actual exposure; overstating a risk teaches the owner to discount warnings.
tripwire: Text corrected; no automated check.
applies_to_new_node: yes — owner-facing warnings on both nodes.

class: knowledge ingested but unreachable by the owner's phrasing
what_happened: After the removal, a direct RAG search returned the new section as the top hit, but asking 'Where is the Terminal page? I cannot find it in the sidebar' answered 'I do not have information about a Terminal page'.
root_cause: Chat intent routing, not ingestion, was phrasing-sensitive (a known knowledge-fragmentation issue).
lesson: Assistant knowledge updates must be verified by asking owner-phrased questions end to end, not by ingest logs or direct retrieval alone.
tripwire: Verified by query (rag/search and a live chat question). Should exist: a fixed set of owner-phrased questions with expected sources run in CI.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the sandboxed assistant.

class: broken read path returns a plausible default instead of an error
what_happened: RB-LND-ANCHOR-CPFP-BUMP-01 read fees from /api/mempool/fees, which does not exist; the 404 body was valid JSON, so .get('fastestFee', 30) fell through to its default. Measured live: 30 sat/vB versus a real fastest fee of 2.11 sat/vB (~14x) for an anchor CPFP bump.
root_cause: A numeric fallback default in a sats-spending path and no HTTP status check before parsing.
lesson: Any code that spends sats (fee bumps, sweeps, channel opens) must fail loudly when its fee source fails: no numeric fallback defaults, HTTP status checked before parsing, and one validated fee endpoint.
tripwire: runbookCommandAudit.test.ts: no invented fee default, no /api/mempool/ endpoints; rewritten fee commands run live and the failure path confirmed to exit non-zero.
applies_to_new_node: yes — both nodes run LND; anchor CPFP and sweeps spend real sats.

class: remediation references nonexistent endpoints and ports
what_happened: Runbooks called a fictional /api/lnd/internal/* family and curled LND REST on :8080, which was the llama-server (LND REST was on 8180), so the unlock runbook TLS-handshaked the inference server; 14 of 89 runbooks were broken.
root_cause: Runbook commands were written against an imagined architecture and never executed or checked against real routes and ports.
lesson: Every runbook command must be statically checked in CI against real endpoints, ports, units, scripts and container names, and its read-only precheck/validate steps must be runnable in an audit (never action/rollback).
tripwire: runbookCommandAudit.test.ts (10 tests with negative controls: no Compose v1, no deleted overlays, no /api/lnd/internal/, no LND REST on :8080, no phantom rikuri-backup units); audit ran 89 read-only commands through a mutation denylist.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any self-heal runbook catalog on the new node.

class: unresolved template placeholder reaches the shell
what_happened: DRB-CONTAINER-CRASHLOOP-01 used {{container}} while the caller supplied only {service}, and the templater's plain .replace() let the literal placeholder reach the shell ('docker inspect ... {{container}}'); {{repo_root}} was registered by nobody.
root_cause: The templater did not fail on unresolved placeholders and runbooks did not declare their parameters.
lesson: The runbook templater must refuse to execute any command still containing an unresolved placeholder, and each runbook must declare the parameters it expects.
tripwire: runbookCommandAudit.test.ts: no unsupplied template variable (honouring each runbook's parameters block); Rust unit test that {{repo_root}} substitutes to an absolute path. Only 7 of 88 runbooks declared parameters at the time.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any templated remediation on the new node.

class: diagnosis built on a phantom component
what_happened: Backup-stale diagnosis read a systemd backup timer that existed under no name (backups run in-process via node-cron), and DRB-BACKUP-STALE-01's highest-prior hypothesis (0.55) depended only on that dead signal and routed to a broken runbook.
root_cause: The architecture moved from systemd timers to an in-process scheduler without updating signals and runbooks.
lesson: Backup freshness must be measured from the actual backup artifacts on each destination, and diagnosis signals must be tied to components that exist.
tripwire: backup.timer.last_run_hours repointed to the newest file under data/backups/config/; runbookCommandAudit.test.ts rejects rikuri-backup systemd units.
applies_to_new_node: yes — backup monitoring on both nodes.

class: dead-code verdict from an incomplete search
what_happened: Three times in one session a 'that's dead' reading was wrong: intelligentRouter's consumers were looked for in index.ts instead of app.ts (two live endpoints and the AI model router would have been deleted), a truncating head -5 hid the LND wallet-password file, and pgrep matched its own command line.
root_cause: Deletion decisions relied on a first-pass grep of the source tree.
lesson: Before deleting code, prove it dead symbol by symbol against all mount/import points and against the live system (endpoints answering, units installed, processes running).
tripwire: Method rule; typecheck caught dangling callers. Should exist: a dead-export check in CI plus a live endpoint inventory.
applies_to_new_node: yes — cleanup work on the new repo.

class: component with missing inputs reports success-shaped zeros
what_happened: knowledgeBase.ts read four JSON files that never existed anywhere and reported 'Knowledge: 0 services, 0 commands, 0 guides' into a status field no frontend read; the generated data/commands.json chain loaded from a nonexistent directory.
root_cause: Missing inputs were treated as empty rather than as an error.
lesson: A component whose required inputs are missing must fail or report degraded, never empty-but-healthy, and generated artifacts with no live consumer must be deleted.
tripwire: Files deleted; typecheck and suite green. Should exist: a startup assertion that each knowledge store is non-empty.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the assistant's knowledge loaders.

class: automation runs without its precondition
what_happened: Runbooks were rewritten onto LND's real mechanisms: wallet unlock via lnd-start.sh passing --wallet-unlock-password-file when the password file exists, cookie resync reduced to a restart because LND reads the bind-mounted .cookie at startup, and watchtower sweep-fee tuning gated on at least one registered tower (the node had none).
root_cause: Earlier runbooks invoked fictional internal routes instead of LND's own mechanisms.
lesson: LND automation must use LND's own mechanisms and be gated on explicit preconditions (password file present, tower registered); when a precondition is absent it must stop and hand the owner the exact remediation.
tripwire: runbookCommandAudit.test.ts; rewritten runbooks.
applies_to_new_node: yes — LND on both nodes; the auto-unlock depends on a wallet password file on disk, which the new node must choose explicitly.

class: control that reports success while doing nothing
what_happened: With the emergency-stop flag set and status reporting aiOperational:false, AI chat still answered and executed tools; the flag had no consumer beyond the routes that wrote and displayed it, and a config field pointed at a different path that nothing read.
root_cause: The stop was implemented as a write path plus a status readout with no enforcement point.
lesson: The AI emergency stop must be enforced at one choke point mounted before all AI routes and in every autonomous loop and the command executor; it must persist across restarts, fail safe on a corrupt flag (treat as stopped), exempt its own stop/resume/status routes, abort in-flight commands, and on resume install a fresh abort signal so aborted work never continues.
tripwire: services/ai/emergencyStop.ts + emergencyStop.test.ts (13 tests: survives simulated restart, aborts the live signal, resume never revives the old signal, corrupt flag fails safe, guard 503s AI work but never blocks /emergency-*, balanced audit). Long-running LLM calls were not yet cancelled mid-flight.
owner_decision: "Once pressed, the AI should stop what it's doing." "If reactivated, it shouldn't continue what it was doing." "Should the activation have a matching deactivation?"
applies_to_new_node: yes — the sandboxed assistant needs a real kill switch.

class: out-of-band state change leaves the audit trail unbalanced
what_happened: A stop cleared out-of-band (script, manual rm, restored backup) logged nothing and left a dangling critical activation.
root_cause: Only the API path wrote audit events.
lesson: Security-relevant state must be reconciled against its audit trail: when the state changes by a path the module did not perform, the module must record the matching event.
tripwire: reconcile() verified live (manual set/clear produced out-of-band ACTIVATED/DEACTIVATED); covered in emergencyStop.test.ts.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any flag-file or on-disk security state.

class: test writes to the production audit log
what_happened: The first run of the new emergency-stop suite, before the audit logger was stubbed, wrote 12 real EMERGENCY_STOP_* entries into /var/log/autonode/ai-security-audit.jsonl; they were disclosed, not deleted.
root_cause: The test used the real audit logger singleton and its production path.
lesson: A test must never write to a live audit log or live data, and audit logs are append-only — never edited to remove inconvenient entries.
tripwire: Suite now mocks the logger; generalized later by per-worker DATA_DIR temp dirs (2026-09-16-backup-truth-and-alerts.md).
applies_to_new_node: yes — tests run on the node machines.

class: authorization scope wider than the decision that granted it
what_happened: Step-up tokens were minted with no binding and checked only for existence and expiry, so a password entered for one benign action produced a token replayable against any step-up route.
root_cause: issueStepUpToken() took no arguments and consumeStepUp() did not compare method or path.
lesson: Action-time credentials must be bound to the exact method and path they were minted for (mandatory, not best-effort), single-use, burned on a wrong-route attempt, and normalized exactly like the gate.
tripwire: stepUpBinding.test.ts (10 tests); live: missing binding returns 400 bind_required.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any action-time owner confirmation on the new node.

class: credential-equivalent data on a public route
what_happened: GET /api/node-connect/info returned the local IP, hostname, OS username and every .onion (dashboard, bitcoin, electrs, lnd, mempool, ssh) with no credential.
root_cause: The route sat under a public-allowlist prefix judged pre-login-safe as a whole.
lesson: The node must treat its onion addresses and connection strings as credentials requiring owner authentication for every method; removing a public prefix is not enough when loginless viewers can still read.
tripwire: apiAccessPolicy.test.ts onion-as-credential cases (70 tests total); live 401 including the re-cased path.
applies_to_new_node: yes — Tor hidden services on both nodes.

class: security control's lifetime tied to an unrelated subsystem
what_happened: The websocket auth middleware (io.use) was registered inside the Notification Manager try{} whose catch logged a 'non-critical' WARN, so a notification-subsystem failure would have left sockets unauthenticated.
root_cause: Auth registration shared an error boundary with an optional subsystem.
lesson: Authentication middleware must fail closed: if it cannot be registered, a replacement must reject every connection.
tripwire: Replacement io.use that rejects every socket on registration failure. Should exist: a test that simulates registration failure.
applies_to_new_node: yes — websocket/streaming endpoints in the rebuilt backend.

class: edit reported success but did not apply
what_happened: An edit to STEP_UP_ALL_METHODS matched on 6-space indentation after the list had been re-indented to 2, so it silently changed nothing (curl still 200); a scripted edit aborted by a later assert left duplicate requires believed removed. Both were caught only by live re-verification, typecheck and re-grep.
root_cause: The edit tool's success was taken as evidence the change applied.
lesson: An edit that reports success is not evidence: every change must be re-verified against the built artifact and the running system, and scripted edits must assert their match.
tripwire: Re-applied with an assert; typecheck, re-grep and live curl.
applies_to_new_node: yes — AI-driven edits on the new repo.

class: test-runner projects diverge and a red gate is misattributed
what_happened: Three script-style files ran under the 'local' jest project (which lacked the unit project's exclusions) and were rejected; their orphaned top-level awaits produced 'rollbackService._saveHistory is not a function', a red herring blamed on in-flight rollback work across several records.
root_cause: The local and unit jest projects applied different include/exclude rules, and the red was attributed by guess rather than diagnosis.
lesson: All test projects must share one include/exclude source, a red gate must be diagnosed before it is attributed, and an empty suite must be declared as counted debt rather than hidden.
tripwire: local project given the same exclusions; passWithNoTests with a comment that live-service coverage was zero.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the new repo's test configuration.

class: derived display outlives the event it describes
what_happened: 'Last update completed successfully.' was derived on every poll from a state file nothing ever cleared, so the green banner was permanent and undated; collapsed, the card showed '0 updates' with no reason because the staged-rollout explanation lived only in the expanded view.
root_cause: There was no expiry concept and no timestamp on a derived success claim, and the explanation was hidden in a collapsed-by-default component.
lesson: Every success claim shown to the owner must carry its timestamp and expire after a bounded window; failures must never fade; an absent or unparseable timestamp keeps the banner; display TTLs must never reach alert-suppression logic; and a card's reason for existing must be visible when collapsed.
tripwire: applyDoneBannerTtl + upgradeDoneBanner.test.ts (19 tests; mutation TTL=Infinity fails 5, removing the asymmetry fails 2), including two tests that the display TTL does not leak into alert suppression.
applies_to_new_node: yes — update status UI for rpm-ostree updates.

class: a lesson without a tripwire recurs
what_happened: loadCards() again silently dropped a concept card (CARD-CONTAINER-CRASHLOOP-01, 53 of 54 loaded) for missing owner/last_reviewed — the same class fixed on 2026-08-10 without a gate.
root_cause: The first fix repaired instances but added no check, so the next hand-written card repeated the defect.
lesson: Every fixed defect class must get a permanent check; the assistant's knowledge cards must be integrity-tested in CI (all load, required fields non-empty, unique ids, offenders named).
tripwire: conceptCardsIntegrity.test.ts (proven red, naming CARD-CONTAINER-CRASHLOOP-01, when the fields are stripped).
applies_to_new_node: yes — the assistant's knowledge store.

class: threshold calibrated to an imagined scale
what_happened: minRelevance 0.5/0.6 assumed a similarity scale all-MiniLM-L6-v2 never produces on this corpus (relevant matches 0.35-0.63), so the live 1318-chunk ChromaDB store was discarded for ~40% (0.5) to ~70% (0.6) of queries, and silently truncated otherwise, while an offline index answered.
root_cause: The constants were chosen without measuring the model's score distribution, guarding a path whose failure a fallback hid.
lesson: Retrieval thresholds must be calibrated on a measured query set for the specific embedding model and corpus, stored with their measurement, and re-measured whenever the model or corpus changes.
tripwire: ai/retrievalRelevance.ts (DEFAULT 0.30, STRICT 0.38) + ragRelevanceCalibration.test.ts (8; restoring 0.5/0.6 fails 2); live primary path served 10/10 queries (was ~6/10). Nothing re-measures automatically on a model change.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the sandboxed assistant will run a small local embedding model.

class: health canary satisfied by the fallback
what_happened: The RAG canary passed whenever sources.length > 0, and the offline fallback always supplied sources, so it reported healthy while the primary store was being bypassed.
root_cause: The canary asked 'did I get an answer' instead of 'did the primary path answer'.
lesson: Every canary must assert which path served the request and fail when a fallback is serving; fallback outcomes must be labelled and counted (filtered, empty, unavailable, error) and the alert must point at the right remediation.
tripwire: ragCanaryBypass.test.ts (5; reverting to ok = gotSources fails 3); forced bypass on the real store (minRelevance 0.99) emitted the warning and lastPath: fallback_filtered.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any primary/fallback pair on the new node (RAG, fee sources, RPC backends).

class: plausible wrong diagnosis committed before measurement
what_happened: The first diagnosis, already committed in another record, blamed the score formula 1 - dist/2; measurement showed the embeddings are L2-normalised, so the formula equals cosine to six decimals, and the threshold was the real defect.
root_cause: A hypothesis was recorded as the cause before it was checked against live data.
lesson: A root cause must be confirmed by measurement before it is recorded or fixed, and a wrong diagnosis already committed must be corrected where it was first recorded.
tripwire: Correction written into both records; tests lock the formula as correct.
applies_to_new_node: yes — debugging practice on the new repo.

class: block-list over a set whose members cannot be named in advance
what_happened: ryzen.local resolved to the Compose bridge address 172.18.0.1 (plus Tailscale and veth addresses), making the node unreachable by name from the LAN after container churn; the existing deny-interfaces=docker0,veth* did nothing.
root_cause: avahi matches interface names literally (no globbing) and Compose bridges are br-<id> with an id that changes on network recreate, so no block-list can work.
lesson: mDNS must publish only on an allow-list of physical interfaces derived at runtime (/sys/class/net/<if>/device), must refuse to write an empty list, and must back up and auto-restore its config if the resolved address is not the LAN address.
tripwire: scripts/rikuri-mdns-interfaces-fix.sh + mdnsInterfaceAllowlist.test.ts (10; mutation: block-list fails 2, hardcoded NIC fails 1, removing the empty-list refusal fails 1).
applies_to_new_node: yes — podman on Fedora IoT also creates virtual interfaces and avahi behaves the same.

class: host configuration hand-edited outside the installer
what_happened: /etc/avahi/avahi-daemon.conf had been hand-edited and was not repo-managed, and the installer installed avahi without configuring it, so every installed node was latent for the same failure; the allow-list is also written once, so a NIC added later is not covered.
root_cause: System configuration lived on the host rather than in the installer/image.
lesson: Every host configuration file the node depends on must be produced by the image/installer and asserted, never hand-edited on one machine, and must be regenerated when hardware changes.
tripwire: Not fixed in this record (installer and regeneration follow-ups open). Should exist: the image ships the config and a test asserts it.
applies_to_new_node: yes — Fedora IoT images make shipping config in the image the default path.

class: schema field authored but never implemented gives a vacuously true gate
what_happened: Four DRBs used symptom_signature.required_any, which the engine's type and gate never read; [].every() was vacuously true, so DRB-BACKUP-STALE-01 always matched and ran RB-BACKEND-RESTART-01, stopping the live dashboard every 30 minutes (156 restarts on 2026-09-14) via systemd watchdog SIGKILL.
root_cause: Silent schema drift between runbook JSON authors and diagnosisEngine.ts; the signal-dependency extractor and the test fixture generator shared the same blind spot.
lesson: A self-heal gate must never pass on an empty or unrecognised predicate set: the engine must reject unknown fields and treat 'no recognised predicates' as no-match, and a destructive remediation must run only when a real signal is present.
tripwire: required_any implemented in the gate and in drbSignalDependencies; diagnosisEngine.test.ts 'required_any guard' block (old guard gives Expected no_match, Received exhausted); darkDrbsFire.test.ts fixture fixed; class gate added in 2026-09-17-drb-schema-gate.md.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any self-heal engine on the new node.

class: absence of symptom accepted as proof of fix
what_happened: On 09-14 one quiet Guardian cycle plus midnight were taken as proof the loop was fixed; on 09-16 NRestarts=75 and 56 more firings showed it never stopped. Real proof was watching the 14:00 tick where the gate returned no_match for the false DRB while a genuine DRB fired in the same batch.
root_cause: Verification relied on a quiet window, and the first fix targeted a signal the gate never consulted.
lesson: A fix is verified only by observing the mechanism decide correctly at the time it is known to fire (a true positive and a true negative in the same run), over a window longer than the failure period, never by a quiet interval.
tripwire: 35-minute live journal monitor across the predicted firing; NRestarts check before and after.
applies_to_new_node: yes — verification practice on both nodes.

class: freshness inferred from the mtime of a conditionally written file
what_happened: The SCB staleness signal read channel.backup's raw mtime (~72 h against a >=26 h threshold), but LND only rewrites channel.backup on channel state changes and mainnet had zero channels, so it was permanently 'stale'.
root_cause: A freshness signal assumed periodic writes from a file that is written only on events.
lesson: SCB freshness must be judged relative to channel state changes or channel count, not wall-clock mtime; a channel-less node's SCB is not stale.
tripwire: scbMtimeHours() returns 0 on a node with zero channels and falls through to the mtime check if the channel count fails.
applies_to_new_node: yes — both nodes run LND and back up the SCB.

class: IPv4-only address-class check while a correct helper sat unused
what_happened: A Mac reaching ryzen.local over IPv6 link-local (fe80::..., macOS's default mDNS resolution) got 136 HTTP 429s across polled endpoints while IPv4 clients got none; this was the second incident in the same spot after a 2026-07-04 IPv4 fix.
root_cause: The rate limiter's LAN/tailnet exemption was a hand-rolled IPv4-only regex while an IPv6-aware isTrustedClientIp helper existed with zero callers.
lesson: Every network-trust decision must go through one tested helper covering IPv4 and IPv6 forms (RFC1918, tailnet CGNAT, loopback, fe80::/10, fc00::/7); no hand-rolled address regexes.
tripwire: rateLimiterLanTrust.test.ts (5 cases including the exact fe80 address, parity with the old IPv4 classes, and a public-IP negative).
applies_to_new_node: yes — LAN and tailnet clients reach both nodes over IPv6.

class: tests excluded from CI rot silently
what_happened: 43 script-style test files had been excluded from every CI path since Phase 3; fsmEngine.test.ts pointed 20 of 23 assertions at a module deleted two months earlier, and three 'LOCAL_ONLY' suites turned out to be fully synthetic. Converting them added 36 suites / 774 tests to CI.
root_cause: Tests outside CI are never run, so their subjects can disappear unnoticed.
lesson: Every test file must run in CI under the standard runner, and a ratchet must hold the count of excluded/script-style tests at zero.
tripwire: Ratchet backend_script_style_tests 43 to 0 locked in scripts/quality-ratchet.json; zero .skip/.only/todo/placeholder asserts (grepped).
owner_decision: Owner decision (2026-09-14): delete the file (fsmEngine.test.ts), after its 3 surviving assertions were shown to duplicate existing coverage.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the new repo's CI.

class: empty configuration list means everything rather than nothing
what_happened: Setting LOCAL_ONLY = [] gave the local jest project an empty testMatch, which jest treats as its broad default patterns; it swept up dist/*.js and reported 990 bogus failures.
root_cause: jest interprets an empty testMatch array as unset.
lesson: When a selection is meant to be empty, use an explicit never-matching sentinel and assert the selected count; never rely on an empty list meaning 'none'.
tripwire: Sentinel pattern ['<rootDir>/__no_local_only_tests__']; test:local reports 'No tests found'.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any test or include/exclude configuration.

class: two subsystems share a directory and naming convention for different schemas
what_happened: DRB-CONTAINER-CRASHLOOP-01.json is an executable runbook (runbook_id, steps) sharing the 'DRB-' prefix and directory with decision-tree DRBs; running darkDrbsFire.test.ts for the first time failed on it, and the first fix (renaming its key to drb_id) was wrong and reverted.
root_cause: diagnosisEngine and runbookEngine glob the same directory and rely on a filename-prefix convention for two unrelated schemas.
lesson: Each schema must live in its own location or carry an explicit, validated type field, and the list of files a loader skips must be asserted exactly so a real item losing its id fails loudly.
tripwire: darkDrbsFire.test.ts filters like loadDRBs() and asserts the skip list is exactly the one known file; the naming collision itself was left open.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the self-heal catalog layout on the new node.

class: ratchet baseline drift tolerated across sessions
what_happened: backend_require_calls sat above its 1304 baseline from at least 2026-08-10 (HEAD 1307) up to 1319 on 2026-08-24, keeping the CI ratchet red and being flagged as 'pre-existing' in many records; on 2026-09-14 per-file attribution found 4 of the +11 were legitimate jest.mock-ordering requires and real fixes drove the counter to 1298.
root_cause: Each session attributed the red to other work and declined to fix it, so a red required gate became normal.
lesson: A red ratchet or CI gate must stop the line and be attributed per file at once; baselines move only through real fixes, legitimate exceptions are recorded, and unrelated improvements must not offset regressions.
tripwire: scripts/quality-ratchet.mjs with locked floors (197/1298/240/44/0 at the time).
applies_to_new_node: yes — the new repo's full gate ratchet.

class: parallel agents edit a shared file
what_happened: While five background agents converted tests in parallel, one briefly edited the shared jest manifest before the instruction not to touch it arrived; it was caught via change notification and corrected.
root_cause: Shared configuration files were not reserved for one coordinator from the start.
lesson: When work is split across parallel agents, shared manifests and configs must be owned by one coordinator and reconciled centrally, and agents must be told up front which files they may not touch.
tripwire: Central reconciliation after all batches; harness change notification.
applies_to_new_node: yes — the new repo is built with parallel agents.

class: god page carrying dead state
what_happened: Settings.tsx (1,142 LOC) was split into per-section components (to 278 LOC) and dead Tor-status and approval-mode state and handlers and copyToClipboard — unread since their tabs were removed — were deleted; verification drove all 10 tabs headless against the live build because no Settings tests existed.
root_cause: Removed features left state and handlers behind in a large page with no tests to expose them.
lesson: Frontend pages must stay under the ~800 LOC cap as per-section components; removing a feature removes its state and handlers, and a verbatim refactor of auth-touching UI must be verified by rendering every section against the real build.
tripwire: tsc, eslint, vite build, vitest 78/78, ratchet frontend_any_casts held at 44, Playwright render of all 10 tabs; no Settings unit tests.
applies_to_new_node: maybe — depends on how the rebuilt frontend is structured.

class: unserialized read-modify-write with parse failure defaulting to empty
what_happened: The hourly and nightly device syncs both wrote backup-config.json at 02:00 with no lock or temp file; on 2026-08-10 the overlap left 12 stray bytes, every reader then returned [] silently, and drive backups stopped for five weeks; two writers would have written {} over the drive selection.
root_cause: Five writers did read, modify, writeFile with no lock and no atomic replace, and parse errors fell back to empty defaults.
lesson: Every persistent config store must serialize writes, write atomically (temp, fsync, rename, preserving mode), keep a last-good copy, repair from the first complete document or last-good with an owner alert, and refuse to write a file it cannot read; 'quarantine and return the default' is a silent data wipe for such files.
tripwire: services/backupDeviceConfig.ts + backupDeviceConfig.test.ts (14; replaying the exact 2026-08-10 bytes and the racing drive-stamp/settings update both fail on the old code); first deploy caught a 664 to 644 mode change from umask, fixed and tested.
applies_to_new_node: yes — config stores on both nodes.

class: prototype pollution through a request-body merge
what_happened: updateBackupConfig merges req.body from PUT /api/storage/...; the rewrite copies own keys only and skips __proto__/constructor/prototype (the old spread was already safe; a naive Object.assign would not have been).
root_cause: Rewriting a merge risked replacing a prototype-safe spread with an unsafe assign.
lesson: Any merge of untrusted request data into stored state must copy own keys only and skip __proto__, constructor and prototype.
tripwire: Prototype test in backupDeviceConfig.test.ts (characterization, passes on old and new code).
applies_to_new_node: yes — if the rebuilt backend is JavaScript/TypeScript.

class: backup success reported without per-destination truth
what_happened: Backups reported success while drive copies were silently skipped or failed: unplugged drives were filtered out, copy errors were a warn, unreadable settings returned [], the report's 'Locations: N' counted the node disk, and notification_on_failure only wrote logger.error.
root_cause: The drive sync returned void and the report counted the wrong destinations.
lesson: Every backup must record per-destination outcomes (synced, failed, not connected), count a drive only if it received every file, alert on failure, config error, no destination or a failed copy, and alert on absence of success (connected and >26 h stale or not writable: HIGH; unplugged >7 days: MEDIUM), one message per problem per 24 h with an all-clear.
tripwire: services/backupHealth.ts + backupHealth.test.ts (19 incl. an I1 replay; old scheduler fails 5, old engine fails 5); restore exercised by decrypting the newest .enc. Alert dedup was still in memory.
applies_to_new_node: yes — backups on both nodes.

class: plaintext secrets copied off-node
what_happened: The hourly config backup synced plaintext config_*.tar.gz archives containing .env (RPC passwords, JWT secret, bot tokens, control-plane tokens) to the USB and SSD drives while the encrypted twin was never copied; local data/backups held plaintext LND wallet_*.db copies at 0644.
root_cause: The drive sync copied the plaintext archive, and local backup permissions were not owner-only.
lesson: Only encrypted archives of secrets and wallet material may leave the node (skipped with a visible status when encryption is off), local backup roots must be owner-only (0700 dirs, 0600 files), and a restore from the encrypted copy must be exercised.
tripwire: backupHealth.test.ts 'encrypted-only config', 'encryption-off skip' and 'local 0600' (fail on the old engine); live: only .enc on both drives, folders 0700.
owner_decision: Owner decision (asked): delete the remaining plaintext archives now; no secret rotation (the USB drive never left the owner's possession).
applies_to_new_node: yes — both nodes hold RPC, LND and assistant secrets.

class: stale channel state kept where it could be restored
what_happened: The backup drive held 96 plaintext channel_db.db.gz copies from an unsafe channel.db backup path removed on 2026-07-24 — stale channel state that must never be restored; removal was offered to the owner.
root_cause: An earlier backup path copied LND's channel database.
lesson: The node must back up Lightning channels only through SCB (static channel backups), never by copying channel.db, and must keep stale channel.db copies out of any restore path.
tripwire: Unsafe path removed 2026-07-24; deletion offered. Should exist: a check that no channel.db copies exist on backup destinations and that restore tooling refuses them.
applies_to_new_node: yes — both nodes run LND.

class: test reaches live system data
what_happened: backupBlockchainGate.test.ts overwrote the live backup-config.json.last-good on every unit run, and runbookEngine.test.ts had written 90 fake TEST outcomes into the live data/outcomes.db since 2026-02-22, auto-blacklisting test_runbook; its stats assertion then went red against the live DB.
root_cause: Modules hard-wired __dirname/../../data, tests ran on the node against real paths, and the store bootstrapped last-good on any read failure instead of only ENOENT.
lesson: A test must never be able to touch live data: every data path comes from one configurable root (DATA_DIR) that test setup points at a per-worker temp dir, and stores bootstrap only on ENOENT.
tripwire: src/tests/setup.ts per-worker DATA_DIR temp dir; ENOENT-only bootstrap regression test; live md5 and mtime unchanged across a full unit run. 26 modules still hard-wired the data path at the time.
applies_to_new_node: yes — tests and agents run on the node machines.

class: retry limit scoped to one call, not persisted
what_happened: max_attempts and cooldown applied only inside one diagnose() call, so a failing hypothesis was retried forever: tapd's start runbook had 'ran but did not fix it' 783 times since 2026-07-11 (48 per day).
root_cause: The attempts array was function-local and drbIntegration kept no state between calls.
lesson: Self-heal must enforce a persisted, cross-cycle attempt budget per hypothesis over a rolling window; when spent, skip that hypothesis and continue down the ladder, escalating only when all are spent, with a success in the window resetting it; the budget query fails open (must not disable self-heal) and escalation dedup fails closed (must not storm).
tripwire: diagnosisEngine.test.ts 'a hypothesis over budget is skipped, not executed' (red pre-fix); live: tapd went from 48 attempts/day to 1/day. Per-DRB windows were later evaluated on history and left at the default (2026-09-17-drb-schema-gate.md).
owner_decision: Budget spent: skip that hypothesis and continue down the ladder (escalate only when all are spent), with a 24-hour rolling window.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any self-heal loop on the new node.

class: attempt recorded after an action that can kill the recorder
what_happened: Attempts were written only after the runbook returned; RB-BACKEND-RESTART-01 stops the dashboard process itself, so ~200 real firings on 09-14/09-16 left no rows.
root_cause: recordPast was called after await execFn(...), which never returns when the remediation kills its own process.
lesson: Every self-remediation must persist an 'attempt started' record (outcome UNKNOWN) before executing and update it afterwards, so a remediation that kills its own process still counts.
tripwire: diagnosisEngine.test.ts 'records the attempt BEFORE running the runbook' and 'one row per attempt' (both red pre-fix).
applies_to_new_node: yes — any remediation that can restart the process running it.

class: declared escalation never implemented
what_happened: rollback.on_total_failure (raise_to_human) and notification.page_on_total_failure were dead schema: nothing ever told the owner 'tried N times, still not fixed'.
root_cause: The fields were authored in runbook JSON while the engine only stuffed the message into a result string.
lesson: When self-heal exhausts its options it must notify the owner with the definition's own severity and message, deduplicated by a persisted sentinel so it survives restarts and cannot loop.
tripwire: 'exhausted pages the owner with the DRB rollback message' test (red pre-fix); __ESCALATED__ sentinel row; tapd's page_on_total_failure:false respected live.
applies_to_new_node: yes — escalation to the owner on both nodes.

class: internal alert path blocked by the node's own auth gate, failure swallowed
what_happened: Guardian notifications were POSTed to the node's own /api/notifications/send, which loginless mode step-up gated: 401 x16 in 72 h (backup agent x29 since 09-10); the fallback route was gated the same way, another target route did not exist (404 swallowed), and healthService's require(...).sendAlert hit a default-only export (TypeError swallowed at debug).
root_cause: In-process alerts were sent over HTTP through the auth gate, and delivery errors were logged at low levels instead of raised.
lesson: Alerts raised inside the node must be delivered in-process (or with a scoped machine credential), an alert-delivery failure must itself be loud, and every alert path needs a test that the message reaches the notification manager.
tripwire: ownerNotificationDelivery.test.ts (34; old heartbeat fails 6, old healthService fails 1). Live Telegram delivery of a Guardian alert was not yet observed at record time.
applies_to_new_node: yes — owner alerting on both nodes.

class: case-sensitive enum lookup with a silent default
what_happened: routingRules[severity] with lowercase 'critical', 'warning' or 'high' fell back to MEDIUM, so critical issues were routed as MEDIUM; one periodic sweep was dashboard-only only by accident of that bug.
root_cause: Severity strings were not normalized before lookup and unknown values defaulted silently.
lesson: Severity must be one normalized enum (case-insensitive aliases, unknown values defaulted with a warning), and each alert source must declare its channels explicitly so normalization cannot create a second, maintenance-blind pager.
tripwire: normalizeSeverity + 10 tests (old notificationManager fails 10); dashboardKnowledgeService pinned to channels ['dashboard'].
applies_to_new_node: yes — alert routing on both nodes.

class: one invalid field rejects the whole notification
what_happened: Telegram rejected a message whose inline button URL was http://localhost:5000/dashboard/approvals, so a CRITICAL electrs approval never reached the owner.
root_cause: Approval links used a localhost URL Telegram refuses, and there was no retry without the offending part.
lesson: Notifications must not carry links the channel cannot open (localhost, .local, loopback, single-label); on rejection the node must resend once without link buttons, and approval links must point at an address the owner can reach.
tripwire: Telegram link filter + resend test (old resend block fails 1); isTelegramUsableUrl table.
applies_to_new_node: yes — external notification channels on both nodes.

class: probe parses CLI output that differs across tool versions
what_happened: The NTP probe's 'timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized,TimeUSec,RTCTimeUSec --value' printed nothing on this systemd, so clock_synchronized was false on every cycle for months; DRB-HOST-CLOCK-DRIFT-01 ran 332 attempts with no success and the NTP runbooks were auto-blacklisted.
root_cause: The comma-separated -p form is not supported by this systemd version; the repeated -p form works.
lesson: Host probes must use invocation forms verified on the target OS version, parse output with tested pure functions, and treat empty output as a probe failure rather than a negative reading.
tripwire: parseNtpSynchronized (pure) + characterization tests; live observe snapshot clock_synchronized: true.
applies_to_new_node: yes — Fedora IoT ships a different systemd version; every timedatectl/systemctl parse must be re-verified there.

class: classifier discards an action class
what_happened: The heartbeat's NON_ACTION_VERBS list included 'alert', so LLM observations such as 'SCB backup is 1800 hours old' were dropped every 30 minutes.
root_cause: AI 'alert' outputs were classified as observations rather than notifications.
lesson: AI alert/notify/inform outputs must become deduplicated owner notifications and must never be sent to the execution plane.
tripwire: ownerNotificationDelivery.test.ts LLM-alert case (old heartbeat fails).
applies_to_new_node: yes — the sandboxed assistant's outputs.

class: rate cap counts only successful actions
what_happened: The heartbeat's restart cap recorded only executed restarts, so ~339 failed tapd restart proposals were made in 24 h (678 restart_service lines, all action=failed).
root_cause: attemptRestart pushed to restartHistory only when the restart executed.
lesson: Restart and retry caps must count attempts, not successes, and the cap's own alert must be deduplicated.
tripwire: ownerNotificationDelivery.test.ts restart-cap case (old heartbeat fails).
applies_to_new_node: yes — any restart cap on the new node.

class: sender treats any HTTP response as delivered
what_happened: Rust services sent alerts with no credential and got 401; constitution.rs logged 'Tampering notification sent' for any response including 401, proposal_engine ignored the response, service_monitor posted to :5001 where nothing listened, approved-proposal notifications always said success even when the action failed, and add_peers was a stub reporting success.
root_cause: Five hand-rolled HTTP senders never checked status, and outcome messages were written independently of the result.
lesson: Every sender must check the delivery result and log 'NOT delivered' on failure, outcome messages must reflect the actual result, and internal delivery must go through one shared client.
tripwire: control-plane/src/dashboard_internal.rs (5 Rust tests incl. 401 returns Err against a real local axum server); live end-to-end Rust-to-owner notification history.
applies_to_new_node: yes — any internal service-to-service alerting.

class: loopback trust behind a reverse proxy
